description:
Speaking of a brutish existence.


We live our lives being told to "make a living." For the last dozens of generations this has had an incredible emphasis, at least here in the Midwest, of the "pull yourself up by your own bootstraps" mentality.


It's a fair way of thinking. Times were hard. For a long time, times were hard. We were warring everything around us just to get out to the sun, to survive. Inside our own bodies the war rages on, the same organisms, every one of them trying to survive, trying to become like us.


There's virtue in finding your way. There is more virtue in understanding your small place, and how much real impact it can have on the path before not just you, but for everything around you, and everything around it.



9/6/2024

description:
Let's get a web-based two-player live-drawing pictionary-type game. This will be hosted at drawit.blahpunk.com and I'll have the files in /var/www/drawit.blahpunk.com.


Matches will work in a round-robin style. When a user visits the page they get a lobby menu listing the current rooms and how many players with the total number of player slots available per room. Users can join a room or create a new room -- rooms disappear when they are empty. Choosing to join a room lets you chose how many players between 2 and 9 and allows setting a 4 numeric digit room code used to access the room, which is empty by default and if not set then anyone can join without a code. If a code has been set for a room then show a lock icon next to those rooms in the room lobby.
title: DRAWIT

description:
I have some apps and portions of my website I want to protect with authentication, allowing specified users only to view certain content, and in some places displaying some content for all users, and allowing editor controls for authenticated users. I need to create a unified approach to these authentications.


My openresty webserver is at 192.168.1.180 and I'm hosting blahpunk.com from here with files hosted from /var/www/blahpunk.com. I have some apps running on 192.168.1.5 that require authentication. I'd like to run the authentication app from 192.168.1.5 and this will be in folder /opt/ezpunker


The authorized oauth url for Google oauth is https://secure.blahpunk.com/authenticate and I'd like to create a https://secure.blahpunk.com/login page which allows using Google Oauth, or can accept a username and password.

description:
Intelligence is the use of innate mental abilities to understand order in systems. Understanding the nature of systems, their limits, their rules, and when those rules and limits are surpassed, involves the utilization of innate intelligence.


You can learn how to use this more effectively. The limitations of any system are only for objects contained within that system, and we may utilize as fact that we are limitless objects, and cannot be contained. Rules exist because limits were tested and broken in a system where there was disorder. Rules in systems do not always tell the truth about the nature of those systems.


The ignorance of the scientific mind is that of a candle in a world full of kindling knowledge. It cannot be contained. Accepting that ignorance, that final, true ignorance, that nothing we know could possibly be as we believe it to be, the infinity of unknowns a well into our own minds, seeking always to be filled -- this is a form of freedom. As our minds wander, vast systems of black holes merge and rearrange in the dark, the challenge is truly to accept all data equally, without judgement.


Any real system is flawed, by gravity riding everything.
title: Gravity of intelligence

description:
And they never saw each other again

9/7/2024


Some time long ago I began thinking of any cut in the skin like the separation of vast universes it is. I don't know at what point I began empathizing with the microscopic world. Probably when it began speaking to me. So, at different times, and not all at once.


We miss the comet coming around like the worm misses the earth, like a crystal of sugar coming around once every hundred-thousandth microsecond, generations for some, eons for others. What have we yet to see above.
